svg.text: claudia — front page: dragging a collection onto a place, proposed

A collection is a private list of documents on any places (D443). Dropping it on a place moves all its documents there — each one on its own terms, because each document has its own owner and password (D20).
Collections stay as they are: afterwards their entries point to the new place.
A · Drag a collection onto a place
The label counts the documents; "…" says a list to review follows.
B · Ctrl: copy all of them
A copy of five documents is five questions at once: they are all in one dialog, see C.
C · Drop: one dialog for the whole collection
Every document gets its own line: whether it can go, what it needs, and what will happen. Nothing starts before Move.
Move the documents of Budget 2027 to Finance server
The collection stays as it is and afterwards lists them on Finance server. Each document moves as it is: sealed, with its whole history and everybody's access.
Try this password on every document
Documents it does not open ask for their own password below.
You are an editor, not the owner.
Only the owner can move it. Tick to copy it instead.
Stays — Finance server keeps no slides
Stays — it is on Finance server already
2 will move · 1 can be copied (not ticked) · 2 stay where they are
D · While it runs, and afterwards
One line per document. A document that fails does not stop the others, and nothing leaves the old place before the new one holds it.
Cancel stops after the document being sent; moved documents stay moved.
Not moved: you are not its owner
Stays: Finance server keeps no slides
Budget 2027 now lists the two moved documents on Finance server.
Dropping a collection on a place is a bulk move; Ctrl means a bulk copy. Both open the same list dialog.
A collection dropped on a collection does nothing (there is no sensible meaning).
One password field for the common case (one person, one password everywhere).
Passwords belong to documents (D20), so there is no way around a per-document check.
What the shared password does not open asks for its own, on the line, in rose until it fits.
Not the owner: the line offers a copy instead of a move; ticking it brings the copy question (sheet 2)
for that line. The copy does not enter the collection by itself: two same-named documents in one
collection would be confusing; the result offers "Add the copy to the collection".
A place that does not keep the document's app, or already holds it, is greyed with the reason.
The summary line is the whole message; the button names what will happen ("Move 2 documents"),
never just "OK". If it is not what she expected she cancels here.
Today's server keeps uploads in memory (at most 16 × 64 MB, import notes). A large collection runs one
document at a time with progress, so the ceiling is per document, not per collection.
Partial results are normal and are not errors: the collection keeps all five, the moved ones now
point to Finance server. Failed lines say why and can be retried from the same dialog.
